speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin our assessment, can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if the pain radiates to your arm, jaw, or back?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture). The history of forceful retching after heavy alcohol consumption followed immediately by chest pain and choking is classic for this life-threatening condition; immediate surgical consultation and imaging are required.
